scope.purpose: Govern tool legitimacy, domain authority, interoperability, and automation boundaries across authoring, manufacturing, controls, documentation, and integration environments.
scope.tool_aware_not_instructional: S9 defines what a tool or automation may be authoritative for and how it must respect governed information boundaries. Tool configuration, UI procedures, deployment instructions, and execution mechanics remain downstream implementation content.
non_goals: No modeling technique or tool tutorial
No submission or acceptance gate definition

requirements.statement: Each governed information domain shall have an explicitly declared authoritative tool or environment, with allowed inputs, authoritative outputs, and prohibited authority shifts defined through governed configuration or registry content.
A tool shall not gain governance authority by convenience, prevalence, legacy use, platform access, or technical capability.

Non-authoritative tools may consume, visualize, transform, or temporarily stage governed information only within declared boundaries and shall not silently become the source of truth for that information domain.
Tool and platform integrations shall preserve traceability, lifecycle continuity, and upstream governance ownership across information exchanges.
Automation shall operate as an execution layer that applies governed standards, registries, transformations, checks, or repetitive operations without creating independent governance authority.
Automation shall not redefine standards, bypass governed review or acceptance, introduce uncontrolled authoritative data, or transfer authority by technical side effect.
Automation that can affect governed information shall be documented, versioned, repeatable, traceable to its governing rules, and registered before production use.
Changes to automation logic, scope, target data, or write behavior shall trigger governed reassessment and registry update before the changed automation is used in production.
Changes to tools, tool authority assignments, integrations, or automation shall preserve governed information continuity and shall follow controlled change management.
New tools may enter the governed ecosystem only when their authority boundaries, integration behavior, information-domain impacts, and change ownership are explicitly defined.
